summary: A 35-foot State Forestry Service tower stood on Mount Jefferson from 1947; the mountain became a state park in 1956 and a 2001 draft bill would let public entities use the fire tower for communications.

facts.status_note: Only a 2001 bill describes the fire tower, as a communications site; no later source was found on its condition.

events.note: 35-foot tower erected by the State Forestry Service.
Mount Jefferson officially became a state park.
Draft bill text lets the state and local public agencies use the fire tower and its site for public communications antennas.

evidence.supports: The tower was 35 feet tall and erected by the State Forestry Service in 1947.
evidence.quote: 1947: a 35-foot tower was erected by the State Forestry Service.

evidence.supports: The 1947 date comes from a 1948 state biennial report.
evidence.quote: (Department of Conservation and Development - 12th Biennial Report - 1948)

evidence.supports: Private citizens donated 26 acres for a public park.
evidence.quote: Private citizens, namely J. B. Hash and H.C. Tucker donated 26 acres of land for a public park

evidence.supports: The park also included 10 acres used as a fire station by the State Forestry Service.
evidence.quote: The Wayside Park contained the original 26 acres plus 10 acres used as a fire station by the State Forestry Service.

evidence.supports: Mount Jefferson officially became a state park in 1956.
evidence.quote: Mt. Jefferson officially became a state park in 1956.

evidence.supports: A 2001 draft bill would let certain public entities use the fire tower at Mount Jefferson for public communications.
evidence.quote: to allow certain public entities to use the fire tower at mount jefferson state natural area for public

evidence.supports: The state could provide space on the tower site to public safety and emergency management agencies.
evidence.quote: the State may provide space at the communications tower site to State public safety and emergency management agencies

corrections.current: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources
corrections.proposed: North Carolina Division of Parks and Recreation (manages the state natural area)
corrections.why: The 1947 tower was built by the State Forestry Service, but Mount Jefferson became a state park in 1956, the park history cites the Division of Parks and Recreation, and the 2001 bill concerns the state parks system and the natural area.

sources.title: A brief history of Mount Jefferson
Senate Bill 1211 (2001), Mount Jefferson state natural area provisions (draft text, version 6)

notes_for_editor: The 1947 date and height rest on one transcription of a 1948 state report. The 2001 bill text is a draft (version 6); enactment was not confirmed, and a search snippet citing Session Law 2002-149 was not fetched, so it is not used. No source ties the 1947 tower to the fire tower the 2001 bill mentions; the story does not claim they are the same structure. No source after 2001 describes the tower, and none says whether visitors may climb it, so no access level is recorded. Search snippets claimed the summit now has a communications tower formerly a fire tower and gave acreage figures; those were not on fetched pages, so they are not used. The Wikipedia page fetched for the mountain mentions no tower.
